    // Element (row, column), zero-based; column indexes into the row vector.
    // Precondition: 0 <= row < 2 and 0 <= column < 2.
    ElementAt(self: Matrix2x2, row: Integer, column: Integer): Number
        => row == 0
            ? (column == 0 ? self.Row1.X : self.Row1.Y)
            : (column == 0 ? self.Row2.X : self.Row2.Y);
```

    // Element (row, column), zero-based, from the row-major component array.
    // Precondition: 0 <= row < NumRows and 0 <= column < NumColumns.
    ElementAt(self: MatrixN, row: Integer, column: Integer): Number
        => self.Components[row * self.NumColumns + column];
```

    //==
    // # Sparse and banded matrix readings
    //
    // Element access and the shape statistics of the storage forms declared in
    // `matrices.types.plato`. Element access on a sparse matrix is a sum over
    // the entries naming that position — the coordinate-list invariant — so a
    // position with no entry reads as zero and duplicate entries accumulate, and
    // concatenating two entry lists is exactly matrix addition.
    //
    // Only relations that follow from the field definitions appear here: factorizing
    // or solving these systems needs a numerical kernel this vocabulary does not
    // declare.

    //==
    // # Sparse element access
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparse_matrix#Coordinate_list_(COO)

    // The value at a zero-based position: the sum of the entries naming it,
    // and zero when no entry does.
    ElementAt(self: SparseMatrix, row: Integer, column: Integer): Number
        => self.Entries.Reduce(0.0, (total, e) =>
            total + (e.Row == row && e.Column == column ? e.Value : 0.0));
```

    // The value at a zero-based position: the banded slot when the position is
    // inside the band, and zero outside it.
    ElementAt(self: BandedMatrix, row: Integer, column: Integer): Number
        => self.IsInBand(row, column)
            ? self.Values[self.BandOffset(row, column)]
            : 0.0;
```
